text:
Funny discovery 🙂: Claude just won’t stick to my code conventions, no matter how I phrase the prompt.

But when it comes to fixing linter errors, he’s flawless 🔧.

That got me thinking 🤔 — for humans too, it’s usually easier to fix something with clear feedback than to get it perfect upfront.

So I tried the same idea with end-to-end tests 🧪: write them first, then let Claude adjust the code until everything passes.
And it worked. Really well 🚀.
Now this has become my go-to workflow.

#AI 
#SoftwareEngineering 
#Leadership 
#DevWorkflow 
#EngineeringManagement 
#AITools
—
P.S. It’s not just me — even Martin Fowler point to the same pattern: give the model a clear target, iterate on concrete feedback, and it improves fast. Sources:
Momentic: How AI Will Bring TDD Back from the Dead (tests as guardrails) — https://lnkd.in/ditdZvPi
Builder.io: Test-Driven Development with AI (practical TDD + AI tips) — https://lnkd.in/dtdNWpWX
Martin Fowler: How far can we push AI autonomy in code generation? (LLMs miss instructions on first pass; fix when reviewing) — https://lnkd.in/dVmSwU-G
